cuts.what: Name it: the Tailzu window's 'Its name' page. The placeholder 'A name of your own' fills with 'Zara' as it is typed, SAVE is clicked and the heading turns from 'Tailzu' to 'Tailzu, or Zara'.

It reads the screen: a Road Runners group chat in Messages. Tailzu marks what it understood: a ring on the group name with the tags THE GROUP and THE RIDE, then a ring round Anthony's 'bent my fork' message tagged ANTHONY'S FORK.

Talk to it: the reply it wrote sits in the message box, is sent and lands as a blue bubble marked Delivered: 'I'm in for the long weekend ride! Anthony, is your fork fixed yet?' (right names, right context).
Select and say the change: a paragraph of lecture notes (Theory of 9 Types of Intelligence) is highlighted, then rewritten in place into three short lines. Held on the clean text.

clips.onScreen: [cut 1] Tailzu (window title) / TODAY INSIGHTS WORDS VOICES TRAIN / ITS NAME / Tailzu (then: Tailzu, or Zara) / Tailzu is its name, and always works. Give it a name of your own too, and call it either while you talk: "Zara, make it formal." / A name of your own (placeholder, then Zara typed) / SAVE / TAILZU ONLY [cut 2] Messages, Road Runners: Search, Darla, Kristina, Rich, Road Runners 9:41 AM Spring training here we come / The long weekend is coming up. Who's down for a ride? / Sounds good! My new frame is finally ready for a test run. Even treated myself to a carbon fiber saddle! / Can we plan for 40-50 miles, depending on the weather and how we're feeling? / Been waiting for this! I'm in / What kind of tires are you running now? / Anthony Wu: Still recovering from the last ride when I bent my fork / tags THE GROUP, THE RIDE, ANTHONY'S FORK / Lol you handled that one like a champ! [cut 3] What kind of tires are you running now? / Still recovering from the last ride when I bent my fork / Lol you handled that one like a champ! / Sophie Sun: Spring training here we come / I'm in for the long weekend ride! (cyclist emoji) Anthony, is your fork fixed yet? (smile emoji) / Delivered [cut 4] Triarchic Theory / Focuses on how people apply knowledge, not just how they gain and store it. / Separates intelligence into three categories: Analytical Intelligence, Practical Intelligence, Creative Intelligence / Theory of 9 Types of Intelligence / (selected) Proposes intelligence consists of 9 distinct types, each representing different ways of processing information. / Types include linguistic, logical-mathematical, musical, visual-spatial, bodily-kinesthetic, interpersonal, intrapersonal, naturalistic, and existential. / Everyone has a unique combination of these intelligences, which can be developed over time. / Some debate whether these are distinct intelligences or just talents. -> Nine kinds of smart: words, logic, music, space, body, people, self, nature and big questions. / Everyone has their own mix, and it can grow. / Some say they are just talents. cuts.what: The meeting as a call in a window on the Mac screen: a whiteboard ('Favourite animal + why') with a fish and a second doodle pixelated as a bleep; four dotted colleagues at the table, nameplates MARKETING, PROJECT MANAGER, INDUSTRIAL DESIGN, INTERFACE. Our dot bot is the one at the right-hand INTERFACE seat.
Small talk, bleeped: the doodle is revealed as a blue dog while the dot bot at INTERFACE steps forward bright, a BLEEP tag over his mouth.
Five minutes of it: the stamp '5 MINUTES ON FAVOURITE ANIMALS' slams onto the whiteboard and an eraser wipes the board clean. The dot bot is still at the right-hand seat.
Cut to the Tailzu notes page: 'Remote control kick-off: price, budget, roles', the plain summary, and the WHAT MATTERED points ringed. The small talk is gone, the point is kept. Held.
